en.marketHeading: What is actually different about marketing in {city}
market: {city} is not one search market, it is two sitting on top of each other. More than three million people in the metropolitan area have French as their first official language, and they do not search in translated English. They use different words, they phrase questions differently, and the results they get back are a different set of competitors than the ones you see when you search in English. If your site and your campaigns exist only in English, you are competing for the smaller half of your own city.

The mistake I see most often in {city} is a French page that was run through a translation tool. It reads as translated, it ranks badly because nobody searches using those exact phrasings, and it costs you credibility with the customer you were trying to reach. French keyword research is its own job. It is not the English list translated, and treating it that way is the single most expensive shortcut available here.

There is also a legal dimension that businesses in the rest of the country do not have to think about. A business with an establishment in Quebec has obligations under the Charter of the French Language covering commercial publications and websites, and enforcement scrutiny tightened as of June 2025. That is not a marketing opinion, it is a compliance question, and it is worth getting a straight answer on before you build anything.
